icse7-integers.title: Integers
icse7-integers.subtitle: Number line, four operations, properties and BODMAS

sheet.title: Integers on the number line
items: a<b\iff a \text{ lies to the left of } b

lessons.title: Integers on the number line
ideas: Integers: $\dots,-3,-2,-1,0,1,2,3,\dots$
On the number line, a number on the right is greater.
The absolute value $|a|$ is the distance of $a$ from $0$.
Every integer $a$ has an opposite $-a$, and $a+(-a)=0$.
formulas: a<b\iff a \text{ lies to the left of } b

examples.question: Which is greater: $-7$ or $-3$?
use: a<b\iff a \text{ lies to the left of } b
steps: $-7$ lies to the left of $-3$ on the number line.

examples.question: Arrange in ascending order: $-5,\ 3,\ 0,\ -8,\ 6$.

lessons.title: Adding and subtracting integers
ideas: Same signs: add the sizes and keep the sign.
Different signs: subtract the sizes and take the sign of the bigger size.
To subtract, add the opposite: $a-b=a+(-b)$.

examples.question: Find $(-12)+7$.
steps: Sizes $12$ and $7$: $12-7=5$. Bigger size $12$ is negative.

examples.question: The temperature is $-4^\circ$C. It rises by $9^\circ$C. Find the new temperature.

experiment.title: Counters and zero pairs
steps: Take red counters for $-1$ and blue counters for $+1$.
Show $(-5)+3$: put 5 red and 3 blue counters.
Remove each red–blue pair. A pair is zero.
experiment.result: Two red counters remain, so $(-5)+3=-2$.

lessons.title: Multiplying and dividing integers
ideas: Same signs give a positive answer. Different signs give a negative answer.
An odd number of negative factors gives a negative product.
Division by $0$ is not defined.

examples.question: Find $(-7)\times(-6)$.
Find $(-3)\times4\times(-5)$.
Find $(-72)\div8$.
Find $(-1)^{5}$, that is $(-1)\times(-1)\times(-1)\times(-1)\times(-1)$.
steps: Five negative factors: odd number, so negative.

lessons.title: Properties and BODMAS
ideas: Integers are closed under $+,\ -,\ \times$ but not under $\div$.
Addition and multiplication are commutative and associative.
Order of operations: Brackets, Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction (BODMAS).
Remove brackets in the order $(\ ),\ \{\ \},\ [\ ]$.

examples.question: Find $25\times(-37)\times4$.
Find $(-15)\times102$.
Simplify $-8+24\div(-6)\times3$.

lessons.title: What is a rational number?
ideas: A rational number has the form $\dfrac pq$, where $p,q$ are integers and $q\ne0$.
Every integer is rational: $5=\dfrac51$.
Standard form: denominator positive, and numerator and denominator have no common factor.
Multiply or divide top and bottom by the same non-zero number: the value does not change.

examples.question: Write $\dfrac{-36}{-48}$ in standard form.
Write $\dfrac{45}{-60}$ in standard form.
Are $\dfrac{3}{-5}$ and $\dfrac{-6}{10}$ equal?

lessons.title: Comparing and ordering
ideas: Write each number with the same positive denominator, then compare the numerators.
Every positive rational number is greater than every negative one.
Between any two rational numbers there are infinitely many rational numbers.

examples.question: Compare $\dfrac{-3}{4}$ and $\dfrac{-5}{6}$.
Arrange in ascending order: $\dfrac{-2}{3},\ \dfrac12,\ \dfrac{-5}{6},\ \dfrac34$.
Find a rational number between $\dfrac13$ and $\dfrac12$.

lessons.title: Operations on rational numbers
ideas: Add or subtract after making the denominators equal.
Multiply numerators together and denominators together.
To divide, multiply by the reciprocal. The reciprocal of $\dfrac ab$ is $\dfrac ba$.

examples.question: Find $\dfrac{-5}{8}+\dfrac{7}{12}$.
Find $\dfrac{-2}{3}-\left(\dfrac{-5}{6}\right)$.
Find $\dfrac{-4}{9}\times\dfrac{15}{-16}$.
Find $\dfrac{-7}{12}\div\dfrac{14}{9}$.

icse7-fractions.title: Fractions
icse7-fractions.subtitle: Types of fractions, the four operations and word problems

lessons.title: Kinds of fractions
ideas: Proper fraction: numerator less than denominator, for example $\dfrac35$.
Improper fraction: numerator not less than denominator, for example $\dfrac74$.
Mixed number: a whole number and a proper fraction, for example $1\dfrac34$.
Equivalent fractions have the same value. Lowest terms: HCF of numerator and denominator is $1$.

examples.question: Convert $3\dfrac25$ to an improper fraction.
Reduce $\dfrac{84}{126}$ to lowest terms.
Arrange in ascending order: $\dfrac23,\ \dfrac58,\ \dfrac34$.

lessons.title: Adding and subtracting fractions
ideas: Change the fractions to the same denominator (use the LCM).
For mixed numbers, change them to improper fractions first.

examples.question: Find $\dfrac56+\dfrac{3}{8}$.
Find $4\dfrac13-2\dfrac34$.
A ribbon is $5\dfrac12$ m long. Ravi cuts $1\dfrac34$ m and then $2\dfrac23$ m. How much is left?

lessons.title: Multiplying and dividing fractions
ideas: Multiply numerators and multiply denominators. Cancel common factors first.
“Of” means multiply: $\dfrac23$ of $45=\dfrac23\times45$.
To divide, multiply by the reciprocal of the divisor.
Simplify with BODMAS. “Of” comes before division.

examples.question: Find $2\dfrac25\times1\dfrac{7}{8}$.
Find $\dfrac34$ of ₹$480$.
Find $3\dfrac34\div1\dfrac14$.
Simplify $\dfrac12+\dfrac34\div\dfrac38\text{ of }4$.

experiment.title: Paper folding for multiplication
steps: Fold a paper into $3$ equal parts across. Shade $2$ parts.
Fold it into $4$ equal parts down. Shade $3$ parts in a second colour.
Count the parts with both colours.
experiment.result: $6$ of $12$ parts have both colours, so $\dfrac23\times\dfrac34=\dfrac6{12}=\dfrac12$.

icse7-decimals.title: Decimals
icse7-decimals.subtitle: Place value, operations, conversions and recurring decimals

sheet.title: Adding, subtracting and multiplying
items: \text{places in } a\times b=\text{places in } a+\text{places in } b

lessons.title: Decimals and place value
ideas: Places after the point: tenths, hundredths, thousandths.
Like decimals have the same number of decimal places. Add zeros at the end to make them like.
To compare, make them like decimals and compare from the left.

examples.question: Write $2.375$ as a fraction in lowest terms.
Write $\dfrac{7}{8}$ as a decimal.
Arrange $0.5,\ 0.48,\ 0.505,\ 0.4$ in ascending order.

lessons.title: Adding, subtracting and multiplying
ideas: Add or subtract with the decimal points in one column.
Multiply as whole numbers. The answer has as many decimal places as the two numbers together.
Multiply by $10,100,1000$: move the point $1,2,3$ places right.
formulas: \text{places in } a\times b=\text{places in } a+\text{places in } b

examples.question: Find $2.4\times0.15$.
use: \text{places in } a\times b=\text{places in } a+\text{places in } b

examples.question: Find $0.0357\times100$.

experiment.title: Decimal grid
steps: Draw a $10\times10$ square grid. The whole grid is $1$.
Shade $5$ more small squares in a new column.
experiment.result: $35$ squares are shaded, so the grid shows $0.35$.

lessons.title: Dividing, and recurring decimals
ideas: Divide by a whole number: divide as usual and keep the point in place.
Divide by a decimal: move the point in both numbers until the divisor is a whole number.
A fraction gives a terminating decimal if its denominator (in lowest terms) has only the factors $2$ and $5$. Otherwise the decimal recurs.

examples.question: Write $\dfrac{5}{6}$ as a decimal.
A wire $14.4$ m long is cut into pieces of $0.36$ m. How many pieces?

icse7-exponents.title: Exponents
icse7-exponents.subtitle: Powers, laws of exponents and large numbers

lessons.title: Powers
ideas: $a^n$ means $a$ multiplied by itself $n$ times. $a$ is the base, $n$ is the exponent.
A negative base with an even exponent gives a positive answer. With an odd exponent, the answer is negative.
Write a number as a product of prime powers: $72=2^3\times3^2$.

examples.question: Find $\left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right)^4$.
Write $648$ as a product of prime powers.

lessons.title: Laws of exponents
ideas: The laws work when the bases are the same.
Any non-zero number to the power $0$ is $1$.

examples.question: Simplify $2^5\times2^3\div2^4$.
Simplify $(3^2)^3\div3^4$.
Simplify $\dfrac{25\times5^4\times t^8}{10^3\times t^4}$.

experiment.title: Paper folding
steps: Fold a sheet of paper in half. Count the layers.
Fold again and count. Do this $5$ times.
Write each count as a power of $2$.
experiment.result: The layers are $2,4,8,16,32$, that is $2^1,\dots,2^5$. Each fold multiplies by $2$.

lessons.title: Large numbers in standard form
ideas: Standard form: $k\times10^n$ with $1\le k<10$.
Count how many places the point moves. Left move gives a positive $n$.

examples.question: Write $3\,84\,00\,000$ in standard form.
Write $5.06\times10^5$ in usual form.
Expand $47{,}305$ using powers of $10$.

icse7-sets.title: Set Concepts
icse7-sets.subtitle: Sets, notation, kinds of sets, subsets and Venn diagrams

lessons.title: Sets and notation
ideas: A set is a well-defined collection of objects. Each object is an element.
$a\in A$: $a$ belongs to $A$. $a\notin A$: $a$ does not belong to $A$.
Roster form lists the elements: $A=\{2,4,6,8\}$.
Set-builder form gives a rule: $A=\{x: x \text{ is an even number}, x<10\}$.
Do not repeat an element in a set.

examples.question: Write $A=\{x: x\in\mathbb N, x \text{ is a factor of } 12\}$ in roster form. Find $n(A)$.
Write $B=\{5,10,15,20,25\}$ in set-builder form.
Write the set of letters of the word ‘ASSESSMENT’.
steps: Letters A, S, E, M, N, T (no repeats).

lessons.title: Kinds of sets
ideas: Empty set $\varnothing$ or $\{\ \}$: no elements.
Singleton set: one element.
Finite set: you can count all elements. Infinite set: you cannot.
Equal sets: the same elements. Equivalent sets: the same number of elements.
Universal set $\xi$: the set that contains all sets in a problem.

examples.question: Is $\{x: x\in\mathbb N,\ 3<x<4\}$ empty?
steps: No natural number lies between $3$ and $4$.

examples.question: $A=\{1,2,3\}$ and $B=\{p,q,r\}$. Are they equal or equivalent?
Is the set of natural numbers finite?

lessons.title: Subsets, complement and Venn diagrams
ideas: $A\subseteq B$: every element of $A$ is in $B$.
$\varnothing$ and $A$ itself are subsets of every set $A$.
Complement $A'$: elements of $\xi$ that are not in $A$.
In a Venn diagram, the rectangle is $\xi$ and circles are the sets.

examples.question: Write all subsets of $\{a,b,c\}$.
How many proper subsets has a set with $4$ elements?

experiment.title: Sorting with hoops
steps: Put two hoops on the floor, one for ‘even’ and one for ‘multiple of 3’. Let them overlap.
Place cards $1$ to $12$ in the correct places.
Cards in neither hoop stay outside, inside the room (the universal set).
experiment.result: $6$ and $12$ go in the overlap. $1,5,7,11$ stay outside both hoops.

icse7-ratio-proportion.title: Ratio and Proportion
icse7-ratio-proportion.subtitle: Ratios, dividing in a ratio, proportion and continued proportion

lessons.title: Ratio
ideas: A ratio compares two quantities of the same kind in the same unit.
A ratio has no unit. Write it in lowest terms.
$a:b$ is greater than $c:d$ if $\dfrac ab>\dfrac cd$.

examples.question: Find the ratio of $75$ paise to ₹$3$.
Which ratio is greater: $3:5$ or $5:8$?
Divide ₹$1800$ between Asha and Binu in the ratio $4:5$.
If $a:b=2:3$ and $b:c=4:5$, find $a:b:c$.

lessons.title: Proportion
ideas: Four numbers $a,b,c,d$ are in proportion if $a:b=c:d$.
$a$ and $d$ are the extremes. $b$ and $c$ are the means.
Three numbers $a,b,c$ are in continued proportion if $a:b=b:c$. Then $b$ is the mean proportional.

examples.question: Are $6,\ 9,\ 10,\ 15$ in proportion?
Find the fourth proportional to $4,\ 10,\ 6$.
Find the third proportional to $4$ and $12$.
Find the mean proportional between $9$ and $16$.

experiment.title: Lemonade taste test
steps: Mix $2$ spoons of syrup in $3$ cups of water. Taste it.
Mix $4$ spoons in $6$ cups. Taste it.
Mix $4$ spoons in $5$ cups. Taste it.
experiment.result: The first two taste the same, because $2:3=4:6$. The third is sweeter, because $4:5>2:3$.

icse7-unitary-method.title: Unitary Method
icse7-unitary-method.subtitle: Direct and inverse variation, time and work

lessons.title: Direct variation
ideas: Find the value of one unit first. Then find the value of the required units.
Direct variation: one quantity increases, the other increases in the same ratio.
More articles cost more money.

examples.question: $12$ pens cost ₹$180$. Find the cost of $20$ pens.
A car uses $8$ L of petrol for $96$ km. How far does it go on $15$ L?
A train covers $200$ km in $2\dfrac12$ h. How long does it take for $340$ km?

lessons.title: Inverse variation
ideas: Inverse variation: one quantity increases, the other decreases in the same ratio.
More workers take fewer days. More speed takes less time.
First find the work for $1$ unit, then divide.

examples.question: $15$ men build a wall in $24$ days. How many days do $20$ men take?
Food lasts $40$ days for $300$ soldiers. After $10$ days, $60$ soldiers leave. How long does the rest of the food last?
steps: Food left lasts $300$ soldiers for $30$ days

lessons.title: Time and work
ideas: If A does a work in $n$ days, A does $\dfrac1n$ of the work in $1$ day.
Add the one-day work of people who work together.
Days $=\dfrac{1}{\text{one-day work}}$.

examples.question: A does a work in $10$ days and B in $15$ days. In how many days do they do it together?
A and B together do a work in $12$ days. A alone does it in $20$ days. How long does B take alone?
Pipe A fills a tank in $6$ h. Pipe B empties it in $9$ h. Both are open. When is the tank full?
A can do a work in $8$ days and B in $12$ days. They work together for $3$ days. Then A leaves. How long does B take to finish?

experiment.title: Fill a bucket
steps: Fill a bucket with one mug. Count the mugs, say $12$.
Use two mugs together, one by you and one by a friend.
experiment.result: It takes $6$ rounds. Double the workers gives half the time: inverse variation.

icse7-percent.title: Percent and Percentage
icse7-percent.subtitle: Conversions, percentage of a quantity, increase and decrease

lessons.title: Percent and conversions
ideas: Percent means ‘per hundred’: $x\%=\dfrac{x}{100}$.
To change a fraction or decimal to a percent, multiply by $100$.
To change a percent to a fraction, divide by $100$ and reduce.

examples.question: Write $\dfrac{3}{8}$ as a percent.
Write $45\%$ as a fraction in lowest terms.
Write $0.065$ as a percent.
Write $12\dfrac12\%$ as a fraction.

lessons.title: Percentage of a quantity
ideas: $x\%$ of $A$ means $\dfrac{x}{100}\times A$.
To find what percent $a$ is of $b$, use the same unit for both.
If $x\%$ of a number is $N$, the number is $N\times\dfrac{100}{x}$.

examples.question: What percent of $2$ kg is $250$ g?
$35\%$ of a number is $84$. Find the number.
In an exam, $40\%$ is the pass mark. Ravi gets $185$ marks and fails by $15$ marks. Find the maximum marks.

experiment.title: Percent on a 10 × 10 grid
steps: Shade $25$ squares in one colour and $40$ in another.
experiment.result: $35$ squares are unshaded, so $25\%+40\%+35\%=100\%$.

lessons.title: Increase and decrease
ideas: Percent change is always on the original value.
An increase of $x\%$ multiplies the value by $\left(1+\dfrac x{100}\right)$.
A decrease of $x\%$ multiplies the value by $\left(1-\dfrac x{100}\right)$.

examples.question: The price of a book rises from ₹$250$ to ₹$290$. Find the percent increase.
A town of $24{,}000$ people falls by $5\%$. Find the new population.
After a $20\%$ increase, a salary is ₹$18{,}000$. Find the old salary.

icse7-profit-loss-discount.title: Profit, Loss and Discount
icse7-profit-loss-discount.subtitle: CP, SP, profit and loss percent, marked price and discount

lessons.title: Profit and loss
ideas: Cost price (CP): the price at which you buy. Selling price (SP): the price at which you sell.
Overheads (transport, repair) add to the CP.
Profit and loss percent are always on the CP.

examples.question: A fan is bought for ₹$1500$ and sold for ₹$1725$. Find the profit percent.
A cycle is bought for ₹$2800$. ₹$200$ is spent on repairs. It is sold for ₹$2700$. Find the loss percent.

lessons.title: Finding SP or CP
ideas: Profit: SP is more than CP. Loss: SP is less than CP.
Use the multiplier on the CP.

examples.question: CP $=$ ₹$640$, profit $=12\dfrac12\%$. Find SP.
A watch is sold for ₹$1530$ at a loss of $15\%$. Find the CP.
By selling $12$ pens for ₹$90$, a man loses $10\%$. How many pens must he sell for ₹$90$ to gain $20\%$?
steps: CP of $12$ pens $=\dfrac{90\times100}{90}=100$, so CP of $1$ pen $=\dfrac{100}{12}$

lessons.title: Marked price and discount
ideas: Marked price (MP) is the price on the label.
Discount is always on the MP.
SP after discount $=$ MP $-$ discount.

examples.question: MP $=$ ₹$2400$, discount $=15\%$. Find SP.
A shirt marked ₹$800$ is sold for ₹$680$. Find the discount percent.
A shopkeeper marks goods $25\%$ above CP and gives a $10\%$ discount. Find his profit percent.

experiment.title: Shop role play
steps: Make price tags for $5$ items with an MP.
A friend buys with a ‘$20\%$ off’ card. Find each SP.
Tell your friend the CP. Find the profit or loss on each item.
experiment.result: The discount is found on the MP, but the profit is found on the CP.

icse7-simple-interest.title: Simple Interest
icse7-simple-interest.subtitle: Interest, amount, and finding P, R or T

lessons.title: Simple interest and amount
ideas: Principal $P$: money borrowed or lent. Rate $R$: interest on ₹$100$ for $1$ year. Time $T$ in years.
Amount $A$ is the principal plus the interest.
Change months to years: $9$ months $=\dfrac9{12}$ year. Change days to years: divide by $365$.

examples.question: Find the SI on ₹$4500$ at $8\%$ per annum for $3$ years.
Find the amount on ₹$6000$ at $9\%$ per annum for $2$ years $6$ months.
Find the SI on ₹$7300$ at $5\%$ per annum from $1$ March to $29$ May of the same year.

lessons.title: Finding P, R or T
ideas: Change the SI formula around to find the unknown.
If the amount is given, find $SI=A-P$ first.

examples.question: At what rate does ₹$2500$ give ₹$600$ as SI in $4$ years?
In how many years does ₹$1600$ amount to ₹$2080$ at $7\dfrac12\%$?
What sum gives ₹$945$ as SI at $7\%$ per annum in $3$ years?
A sum doubles itself in $8$ years at SI. Find the rate.
A sum amounts to ₹$3360$ in $2$ years and ₹$3900$ in $5$ years at SI. Find the sum and the rate.
steps: SI for $3$ years $=540$, so for $1$ year $=180$

experiment.title: Bank passbook
steps: Look at a bank passbook or a deposit receipt at home.
Note the principal, the rate and the time.
Find the interest with the formula and compare with the receipt.
experiment.result: The receipt interest matches $\dfrac{PRT}{100}$ for simple interest deposits.

icse7-speed-distance-time.title: Speed, Distance and Time
icse7-speed-distance-time.subtitle: Speed, unit conversion, average speed and trains

lessons.title: Speed, distance and time
ideas: Speed is the distance covered in one unit of time.
Use the same units: km with hours, m with seconds.
To change km/h to m/s, multiply by $\dfrac5{18}$. To change m/s to km/h, multiply by $\dfrac{18}5$.

examples.question: A bus covers $240$ km in $4$ h $48$ min. Find its speed.
Change $72$ km/h to m/s.
A boy walks at $5$ km/h. How long does he take for $1.5$ km?

experiment.title: Your walking speed
steps: Mark $50$ m in the school ground.
Walk the distance. A friend times you with a stopwatch.
Find your speed in m/s and in km/h.
experiment.result: For example, $50$ m in $40$ s is $1.25$ m/s $=4.5$ km/h.

lessons.title: Average speed
ideas: Average speed is total distance divided by total time.
It is not the average of the two speeds, unless the times are equal.

examples.question: A car goes $120$ km at $40$ km/h and the next $120$ km at $60$ km/h. Find the average speed.
A man cycles for $2$ h at $15$ km/h and walks for $1$ h at $6$ km/h. Find his average speed.

lessons.title: Trains and relative speed
ideas: A train passing a pole covers its own length.
A train passing a platform or bridge covers its length plus the platform length.
Same direction: subtract the speeds. Opposite directions: add the speeds.

examples.question: A train $180$ m long passes a pole in $12$ s. Find its speed in km/h.
A train $240$ m long runs at $54$ km/h. How long does it take to cross a bridge $360$ m long?
Two trains $150$ m and $100$ m long run in opposite directions at $50$ km/h and $40$ km/h. How long do they take to cross each other?

icse7-algebra.title: Fundamental Concepts
icse7-algebra.subtitle: Terms, like terms, operations on expressions and substitution

sheet.title: Terms and expressions
items: \text{Like terms: same variables with the same powers}

lessons.title: Terms and expressions
ideas: A variable is a letter that stands for a number. A constant has a fixed value.
A term is a number, a variable, or their product. Terms are joined by $+$ or $-$.
The number part of a term is its coefficient: in $-7x^2y$ the coefficient is $-7$.
Monomial: one term. Binomial: two terms. Trinomial: three terms. Polynomial: one or more terms.
The degree of a polynomial is the highest power of the variable.
formulas: \text{Like terms: same variables with the same powers}

examples.question: In $5x^2-3xy+7$, name the terms and the coefficient of $xy$.
Pick the like terms: $3ab,\ -5a^2b,\ 7ba,\ 2ab^2,\ -ab$.
use: \text{Like terms: same variables with the same powers}

examples.question: Write the degree of $4x^3-2x^5+x-9$.

lessons.title: Adding and subtracting expressions
ideas: Add or subtract only like terms. Add their coefficients.
To subtract, change the sign of every term being subtracted, then add.
Remove brackets: a minus sign in front changes every sign inside.

examples.question: Subtract $4a-7b+3c$ from $6a-2b-5c$.
Simplify $5x-[3y-\{2x-(y-x)\}]$.

lessons.title: Multiplying and dividing; substitution
ideas: Multiply coefficients and add powers of the same variable.
Multiply each term of one bracket by each term of the other.
To divide by a monomial, divide each term.
Substitution: put the given values in place of the variables, then use BODMAS.

examples.question: Find $(-3x^2y)\times(4xy^3)$.
Divide $12x^3-8x^2+4x$ by $4x$.
Find $a^2-2ab+3b^2$ when $a=-2$ and $b=3$.

sheet.title: Word problems
items: \text{consecutive even or odd: } x,\ x+2,\ x+4

lessons.title: Solving an equation
ideas: An equation has an equal sign. A linear equation has the variable only with power $1$.
Do the same operation on both sides. The balance stays level.
Transpose: a term moves to the other side with the opposite operation.
Check the answer by putting it back in the equation.

examples.question: Solve $3x-7=11$.
Solve $\dfrac{x}{3}+\dfrac{x}{4}=14$.
Solve $\dfrac{2x-1}{3}-\dfrac{x+2}{4}=1$.

experiment.title: Balance with cups
steps: Put $3$ closed cups with the same number of marbles and $2$ loose marbles on the left pan.
Put $14$ loose marbles on the right pan. The pans balance.
Take $2$ marbles off each pan, then share the rest in $3$ groups.
experiment.result: $3x+2=14$, so $3x=12$ and $x=4$. Each cup has $4$ marbles.

lessons.title: Word problems
ideas: Let the unknown be $x$. Write the equation from the words.
Solve it and answer the question in words with units.
formulas: \text{consecutive even or odd: } x,\ x+2,\ x+4

examples.question: The sum of three consecutive numbers is $72$. Find them.
A father is $3$ times as old as his son. In $12$ years he will be twice as old. Find their ages.
The length of a rectangle is $5$ cm more than its breadth. Its perimeter is $50$ cm. Find the sides.
Ravi has ₹$500$ in ₹$10$ and ₹$20$ notes, $35$ notes in all. How many of each?

icse7-inequalities.title: Inequalities
icse7-inequalities.subtitle: Inequations, replacement set, solution set and the number line

sheet.title: Inequations and sets
items: x<a:\ x \text{ is less than } a
x\le a:\ x \text{ is less than or equal to } a

lessons.title: Inequations and sets
ideas: An inequation uses $<,\ >,\ \le$ or $\ge$, for example $x+3<7$.
The replacement set is the set from which $x$ can take values.
The solution set is the set of values in the replacement set that make the inequation true.
$\mathbb N=\{1,2,3,\dots\}$, $\mathbb W=\{0,1,2,\dots\}$, $\mathbb Z=\{\dots,-1,0,1,\dots\}$.
formulas: x<a:\ x \text{ is less than } a
x\le a:\ x \text{ is less than or equal to } a

examples.question: Solve $x+3<7$, $x\in\mathbb N$.

lessons.title: Rules for solving
ideas: Add or subtract the same number on both sides: the sign stays.
Multiply or divide both sides by a positive number: the sign stays.
Multiply or divide both sides by a negative number: the sign reverses.

examples.question: Solve $3x-5\le10$, $x\in\mathbb W$.
Solve $-2x>6$, $x\in\mathbb Z$.
Solve $-3\le 2x+1<7$, $x\in\mathbb Z$.
Solve $\dfrac{x}{2}+1>\dfrac{x}{3}+2$, $x\in\mathbb N$, $x\le10$.

experiment.title: Number line walk
steps: Draw a number line from $-5$ to $5$ on the floor with chalk.
Stand on each integer and say if $2x+1<5$ is true.
Mark the true points with a dot.
experiment.result: The dots are at $\dots,-2,-1,0,1$. All integers less than $2$ work.

lessons.title: Graphing on the number line
ideas: For integers, mark the solution set with solid dots.
For real numbers, a filled dot means the end value is included and an open dot means it is not.
Draw a thick line between the end points for real numbers.

examples.question: Show $x\in\mathbb Z$, $-1<x\le3$ on a number line.
Show $x\in\mathbb R$, $-2\le x<1$.
steps: Filled dot at $-2$, open dot at $1$, thick line between

icse7-lines-angles.title: Lines and Angles
icse7-lines-angles.subtitle: Pairs of angles, transversals and parallel lines

lessons.title: Pairs of angles
ideas: Complementary angles add up to $90^\circ$. Supplementary angles add up to $180^\circ$.
Adjacent angles have a common vertex and a common arm, and no common inside points.
A linear pair is two adjacent angles on a straight line. They add up to $180^\circ$.
Vertically opposite angles are equal.
Angles at a point add up to $360^\circ$.

examples.question: Find the complement of $37^\circ$ and the supplement of $112^\circ$.
Two supplementary angles are in the ratio $4:5$. Find them.
An angle is $24^\circ$ more than its complement. Find it.
Two lines cross. One angle is $3x+10^\circ$ and the vertically opposite angle is $5x-30^\circ$. Find $x$ and all four angles.

lessons.title: Parallel lines and a transversal
ideas: A transversal cuts two or more lines at different points.
If the lines are parallel:
corresponding angles are equal,
alternate interior angles are equal,
co-interior angles (same side) add up to $180^\circ$.
If any one of these is true, the lines are parallel.

examples.question: $AB\parallel CD$ and a transversal makes $\angle1=65^\circ$ at $AB$. Find the corresponding angle and the co-interior angle at $CD$.
Co-interior angles are $(2x+15)^\circ$ and $(3x-10)^\circ$. Find $x$.
Two lines are cut by a transversal. The alternate angles are $72^\circ$ and $72^\circ$. Are the lines parallel?

experiment.title: Folding parallel lines
steps: Fold a sheet of paper once. Fold it again parallel to the first fold.
Draw a slanting line across both folds.
Measure the eight angles with a protractor.
experiment.result: Four angles are equal and the other four are equal. Each acute angle and obtuse angle add up to $180^\circ$.

icse7-triangles.title: Triangles
icse7-triangles.subtitle: Kinds of triangles, angle sum, exterior angle and inequalities

lessons.title: Kinds of triangles
ideas: By sides: scalene (no equal sides), isosceles (two equal sides), equilateral (three equal sides).
By angles: acute-angled, right-angled, obtuse-angled.
In an isosceles triangle, the angles opposite the equal sides are equal.
Each angle of an equilateral triangle is $60^\circ$.

examples.question: In $\triangle ABC$, $AB=AC$ and $\angle A=40^\circ$. Find $\angle B$.
Name the triangle with angles $35^\circ$, $55^\circ$, $90^\circ$.
steps: One angle is $90^\circ$. All angles are different.

lessons.title: Angle sum and exterior angle
ideas: The three angles of a triangle add up to $180^\circ$.
An exterior angle equals the sum of the two interior opposite angles.
An exterior angle is greater than each interior opposite angle.

examples.question: The angles of a triangle are in the ratio $2:3:4$. Find them.
An exterior angle of a triangle is $110^\circ$. One interior opposite angle is $45^\circ$. Find the other two angles.
In $\triangle ABC$, $\angle A=x$, $\angle B=2x$ and $\angle C=x+20^\circ$. Find each angle.

experiment.title: Tear the corners
steps: Cut a triangle from paper. Mark its corners $1,2,3$.
Place them side by side at one point on a straight line.
experiment.result: The three corners make a straight angle: $\angle1+\angle2+\angle3=180^\circ$.

lessons.title: Sides and angles
ideas: The sum of any two sides is greater than the third side.
The difference of any two sides is less than the third side.
The greatest angle is opposite the greatest side. The smallest angle is opposite the smallest side.

examples.question: Can $4$ cm, $7$ cm and $12$ cm be the sides of a triangle?
Two sides of a triangle are $5$ cm and $9$ cm. Find the range of the third side.
In $\triangle PQR$, $PQ=6$, $QR=8$, $PR=5$ cm. Name the greatest and the smallest angle.
steps: Greatest side $QR$ is opposite $\angle P$. Smallest side $PR$ is opposite $\angle Q$.

icse7-pythagoras.title: Pythagoras Theorem
icse7-pythagoras.subtitle: The theorem, its converse and applications

lessons.title: The theorem
ideas: In a right-angled triangle, the side opposite the right angle is the hypotenuse. It is the longest side.
The square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides.

examples.question: The legs of a right triangle are $9$ cm and $12$ cm. Find the hypotenuse.
The hypotenuse is $26$ cm and one side is $10$ cm. Find the other side.
Find the diagonal of a rectangle $15$ cm by $8$ cm.

experiment.title: Squares on the sides
steps: Draw a right triangle with sides $3$ cm and $4$ cm on squared paper.
Draw a square on each side and count the unit squares.
Compare the big square with the two small squares.
experiment.result: $9+16=25$, so the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the other two.

lessons.title: The converse and triplets
ideas: If $c^2=a^2+b^2$ for the longest side $c$, the triangle is right-angled.
A Pythagorean triplet is three natural numbers with $a^2+b^2=c^2$.
Multiples of a triplet are also triplets.

examples.question: Is a triangle with sides $7$, $24$, $25$ right-angled?
Is a triangle with sides $6$, $9$, $11$ right-angled?
Write a triplet with $m=4$.

lessons.title: Applications
ideas: Draw a figure. Find the right angle. Then use the theorem.
A ladder against a wall: the ladder is the hypotenuse.

examples.question: A $13$ m ladder reaches a window $12$ m high. How far is its foot from the wall?
A man goes $16$ km east and then $12$ km north. How far is he from the start?
The diagonals of a rhombus are $16$ cm and $30$ cm. Find a side.
steps: Diagonals bisect at right angles: halves $8$ and $15$

examples.question: Two poles $11$ m and $6$ m high stand $12$ m apart. Find the distance between their tops.

icse7-symmetry.title: Symmetry
icse7-symmetry.subtitle: Lines of symmetry, rotational symmetry and order

lessons.title: Line symmetry
ideas: A figure has line symmetry if one half folds exactly onto the other half.
The fold line is the line (axis) of symmetry.
A regular polygon with $n$ sides has $n$ lines of symmetry.
A circle has infinitely many lines of symmetry.

examples.question: How many lines of symmetry has a rectangle (not a square)?
steps: One through the middles of the long sides, one through the middles of the short sides. The diagonals do not work.

examples.question: How many lines of symmetry has a regular hexagon?
Which capital letters among A, B, H, N, S, X have a vertical line of symmetry?
steps: A, H, X fold left onto right. B folds top onto bottom only. N and S have none.

experiment.title: Ink blot
steps: Fold a sheet in half and open it.
Drop some ink or paint on one side near the fold.
experiment.result: The pattern is the same on both sides. The fold is the line of symmetry.

lessons.title: Rotational symmetry
ideas: A figure has rotational symmetry if it looks the same after a turn of less than $360^\circ$ about its centre.
The order is the number of times it looks the same in one full turn.
Angle of rotation $=\dfrac{360^\circ}{\text{order}}$.
Every figure looks the same after $360^\circ$. If that is the only time, the order is $1$ (no rotational symmetry).

examples.question: Find the order and the angle of rotational symmetry of a square.
Find the order of rotational symmetry of the letter S.
Does an isosceles triangle (not equilateral) have rotational symmetry?
steps: It looks the same only after $360^\circ$.
examples.result: No (order $1$), but it has $1$ line of symmetry

icse7-solids.title: Recognition of Solids
icse7-solids.subtitle: Faces, edges and vertices, Euler's formula and nets

sheet.title: Solids and their parts
items: \text{Prism with } n\text{-gon base: } F=n+2,\ V=2n,\ E=3n
\text{Pyramid with } n\text{-gon base: } F=n+1,\ V=n+1,\ E=2n

lessons.title: Solids and their parts
ideas: A solid has length, breadth and height.
A face is a flat surface. An edge is where two faces meet. A vertex is a corner.
A prism has two equal and parallel ends and rectangular side faces.
A pyramid has one base and triangular side faces that meet at a point.
A cylinder, cone and sphere have curved surfaces.
formulas: \text{Prism with } n\text{-gon base: } F=n+2,\ V=2n,\ E=3n
\text{Pyramid with } n\text{-gon base: } F=n+1,\ V=n+1,\ E=2n

examples.question: Find $F$, $V$, $E$ for a cuboid.
use: \text{Prism with } n\text{-gon base: } F=n+2,\ V=2n,\ E=3n

examples.question: Find $F$, $V$, $E$ for a pentagonal pyramid.
use: \text{Pyramid with } n\text{-gon base: } F=n+1,\ V=n+1,\ E=2n

examples.question: Find $F$, $V$, $E$ for a triangular prism.

lessons.title: Euler's formula and nets
ideas: For any solid with flat faces (polyhedron), $F+V-E=2$.
A net is a flat shape that folds into a solid.
A cube has $11$ different nets.

examples.question: Check Euler's formula for a cube.
A polyhedron has $12$ faces and $30$ edges. Find the number of vertices.
Can a polyhedron have $10$ faces, $20$ edges and $15$ vertices?

experiment.title: Straws and clay
steps: Use straws for edges and clay balls for vertices.
Build a cube, a square pyramid and a triangular prism.
Count $F$, $V$ and $E$ for each and work out $F+V-E$.
experiment.result: Every model gives $F+V-E=2$.

icse7-congruency.title: Congruency: Congruent Triangles
icse7-congruency.subtitle: Congruence and the SSS, SAS, ASA and RHS conditions

sheet.title: Congruent figures
items: \angle A=\angle P,\ \angle B=\angle Q,\ \angle C=\angle R

lessons.title: Congruent figures
ideas: Two figures are congruent if they have the same shape and the same size.
Congruent figures cover each other exactly.
$\triangle ABC\cong\triangle PQR$ means $A\leftrightarrow P$, $B\leftrightarrow Q$, $C\leftrightarrow R$.
Corresponding parts of congruent triangles are equal (CPCT).
formulas: \angle A=\angle P,\ \angle B=\angle Q,\ \angle C=\angle R

examples.question: $\triangle ABC\cong\triangle XYZ$. Write the parts equal to $BC$ and $\angle C$.
Two line segments are congruent. One is $5.6$ cm. Find the other.

experiment.title: Trace and cover
steps: Draw a triangle on paper and cut it out.
Use it as a stencil to draw a second triangle.
Place one on the other in different ways.
experiment.result: They cover each other exactly when the matching corners meet: the triangles are congruent.

lessons.title: Conditions for congruence
ideas: SSS: three sides of one triangle equal three sides of the other.
SAS: two sides and the included angle are equal.
ASA: two angles and the included side are equal. (AAS also works.)
RHS: right angle, hypotenuse and one side are equal.
AAA does not prove congruence. Triangles can have the same angles but different sizes.

examples.question: In $\triangle ABC$ and $\triangle PQR$, $AB=PQ=5$, $BC=QR=7$, $\angle B=\angle Q=50^\circ$. Are they congruent?
steps: Two sides and the included angle are equal.

examples.question: $AB=AC$ and $AD$ is the bisector of $\angle A$ in $\triangle ABC$. Show that $BD=DC$.
steps: In $\triangle ABD$ and $\triangle ACD$: $AB=AC$, $\angle BAD=\angle CAD$, $AD=AD$

examples.question: In right triangles $ABC$ and $DEF$, $\angle B=\angle E=90^\circ$, $AC=DF=13$ and $AB=DE=5$. Are they congruent?
steps: Right angle, hypotenuse and one side are equal.

examples.question: $\angle A=\angle P=60^\circ$, $\angle B=\angle Q=70^\circ$, $AB=PQ=6$ cm. Find $\angle C$ and state the condition.

icse7-constructions.title: Constructions
icse7-constructions.subtitle: Perpendiculars, bisectors, angles, parallel lines and triangles

lessons.title: Bisectors and perpendiculars
ideas: Use only a ruler and compasses. Do not rub out the arcs.
The perpendicular bisector of $AB$ cuts $AB$ at its midpoint at $90^\circ$.
An angle bisector divides an angle into two equal angles.

examples.question: Draw the perpendicular bisector of $AB=6$ cm.
steps: Centre $A$, radius more than $3$ cm: draw arcs above and below $AB$.
Centre $B$, same radius: arcs cut the first ones at $P$ and $Q$.

examples.question: Bisect $\angle ABC=70^\circ$.
steps: Centre $B$: an arc cuts $BA$ at $D$ and $BC$ at $E$.
Centres $D$ and $E$, same radius: arcs meet at $F$.

experiment.title: Paper folding
steps: Draw a line segment $AB$ on tracing paper.
Fold so that $A$ falls on $B$. Crease and open.
Measure the angle between the crease and $AB$.
experiment.result: The crease is the perpendicular bisector: it meets $AB$ at its midpoint at $90^\circ$.

lessons.title: Special angles
ideas: $60^\circ$: arc from the vertex, then the same radius from the cut point.
$120^\circ$: two $60^\circ$ steps on the same arc.
$90^\circ$: bisect between $60^\circ$ and $120^\circ$.
$30^\circ$, $45^\circ$, $15^\circ$: bisect $60^\circ$, $90^\circ$, $30^\circ$.
$75^\circ$: bisect between $60^\circ$ and $90^\circ$. $135^\circ$: bisect between $90^\circ$ and $180^\circ$.

examples.question: Construct $\angle ABC=60^\circ$.
steps: Centre $D$, same radius: arc cuts the first arc at $E$.

examples.question: Construct $75^\circ$.
steps: Make $60^\circ$ and $90^\circ$ at the same point.

lessons.title: Parallel lines and triangles
ideas: To draw a line through $P$ parallel to $AB$: copy an angle so that corresponding (or alternate) angles are equal.
A triangle can be drawn from SSS, SAS, ASA or RHS.
First draw a rough figure with the given parts marked.

examples.question: Construct $\triangle ABC$ with $AB=5$ cm, $BC=6$ cm, $CA=4.5$ cm.
steps: Centre $B$, radius $5$ cm: arc. Centre $C$, radius $4.5$ cm: arc. They meet at $A$.

examples.question: Construct $\triangle PQR$ with $QR=5.5$ cm, $\angle Q=60^\circ$, $\angle R=45^\circ$.
Construct a right triangle with hypotenuse $6$ cm and one side $4$ cm.
steps: Centre $C$, radius $6$ cm: arc cuts the perpendicular at $A$.

examples.question: Draw a line through $P$ parallel to $AB$.
steps: At $P$, copy $\angle PQB$ in the corresponding position.
The new arm through $P$ is the parallel line.

icse7-mensuration.title: Mensuration
icse7-mensuration.subtitle: Perimeter and area of plane figures, circles, and volume of cuboids

lessons.title: Rectangles, squares and paths
ideas: Perimeter is the length of the boundary. Area is the region inside.
Use the same unit for all lengths. $1\text{ m}^2=10\,000\text{ cm}^2$.
Path area $=$ outer area $-$ inner area.

examples.question: A rectangle is $18$ m by $12$ m. Find its perimeter and area.
The diagonal of a square is $10$ cm. Find its area.
A garden $30$ m by $20$ m has a path $2$ m wide all round it outside. Find the area of the path.
Two cross roads, each $3$ m wide, run through the middle of a park $50$ m by $40$ m, parallel to its sides. Find their area.

lessons.title: Triangles, parallelograms and trapeziums
ideas: The height is perpendicular to the base.
Any side of a parallelogram can be the base, with its own height.

examples.question: Find the area of a triangle with base $14$ cm and height $9$ cm.
A parallelogram has base $12$ cm and area $84\text{ cm}^2$. Find its height.
The parallel sides of a trapezium are $15$ cm and $9$ cm. The distance between them is $8$ cm. Find its area.
The diagonals of a rhombus are $16$ cm and $12$ cm. Find its area.

lessons.title: Circles
ideas: Circumference is the perimeter of a circle. Take $\pi=\dfrac{22}{7}$ unless told otherwise.
In one turn, a wheel moves a distance equal to its circumference.
Semicircle perimeter $=\pi r+2r$.

examples.question: Find the circumference and area of a circle of radius $14$ cm.
The circumference of a circle is $132$ cm. Find its area.
A wheel has diameter $70$ cm. How many turns does it make in $1.1$ km?
Find the perimeter of a semicircle of radius $7$ cm.

experiment.title: String and a can
steps: Wrap a string once round a can. Measure the string.
Measure the diameter of the can.
Divide the string length by the diameter.
experiment.result: The answer is close to $3.14$, that is $\pi$.

lessons.title: Volume of cuboid and cube
ideas: Volume is the space inside a solid.
$1\text{ L}=1000\text{ cm}^3$ and $1\text{ m}^3=1000$ L.

examples.question: Find the volume of a tank $2$ m by $1.5$ m by $1$ m in litres.
Find the volume and surface area of a cube of edge $6$ cm.
How many bricks $25$ cm $\times12.5$ cm $\times7.5$ cm make a wall $10$ m $\times30$ cm $\times1.5$ m?

icse7-data-handling.title: Data Handling
icse7-data-handling.subtitle: Tally tables, mean, median, mode, bar graphs and pie charts

lessons.title: Organising data
ideas: Raw data is data as collected. Arrange it in a frequency table with tally marks.
Range $=$ highest value $-$ lowest value.
A bar graph shows data with bars of equal width and equal gaps.

examples.question: Marks: $7,5,8,7,6,9,7,5,8,7$. Make a frequency table and find the range.

lessons.title: Mean, median and mode
ideas: Mean is the sum divided by the number of values.
Median is the middle value after arranging in order.
If the number of values is even, the median is the mean of the two middle values.
Mode is the value that occurs most often.

examples.question: Find the mean of $12,15,18,20,25$.
Find the median of $8,3,11,6,9,4,7$.
Find the median of $14,9,21,17,10,12$.
Find the mode of $3,5,2,5,7,3,5,8$.
The mean of $6$ numbers is $15$. One number is removed and the mean becomes $14$. Find the removed number.

lessons.title: Pie charts
ideas: A pie chart shows parts of a whole as sectors of a circle.
The whole circle is $360^\circ$.

examples.question: A family earns ₹$36{,}000$: food ₹$12{,}000$, rent ₹$9000$, education ₹$6000$, savings ₹$9000$. Find the angles of the pie chart.

experiment.title: Class survey
steps: Make a tally table and a bar graph.
Find the angle for each sport and draw a pie chart.
experiment.result: The angles add up to $360^\circ$ and the bar heights add up to $20$.

icse7-probability.title: Probability
icse7-probability.subtitle: Experiments, outcomes, events and the probability of an event

sheet.title: Probability of an event
items: P(E)=\dfrac{\text{number of favourable outcomes}}{\text{total number of outcomes}}

lessons.title: Experiments and outcomes
ideas: A random experiment has outcomes that we cannot predict for sure. Example: tossing a coin.
The sample space is the set of all outcomes.
An event is a set of one or more outcomes.
Equally likely outcomes have the same chance.

examples.question: Write the sample space for tossing two coins.
A die is thrown. List the outcomes of the event ‘a prime number’.

lessons.title: Probability of an event
ideas: Probability measures the chance of an event, from $0$ to $1$.
An impossible event has probability $0$. A sure event has probability $1$.
$P(\text{not } E)=1-P(E)$.
formulas: P(E)=\dfrac{\text{number of favourable outcomes}}{\text{total number of outcomes}}

examples.question: A die is thrown. Find $P(\text{even number})$.
use: P(E)=\dfrac{\text{number of favourable outcomes}}{\text{total number of outcomes}}

examples.question: A bag has $5$ red, $3$ blue and $2$ green balls. One ball is drawn. Find $P(\text{blue})$ and $P(\text{not blue})$.
A card is drawn from $1$ to $20$. Find $P(\text{multiple of }3)$.
Two coins are tossed. Find $P(\text{at least one head})$.

experiment.title: Toss a coin 50 times
steps: Toss a coin $50$ times. Record H or T with tally marks.
Join the results of the whole class.
experiment.result: Each result is near $\dfrac12$. With more tosses, the class result comes closer to $\dfrac12$.
